From f0f75a3d98b7959a8677b6363e23190f3018636b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Gunnar Kudrjavets <gunnarku@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 03:00:03 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] tpm2-sessions: Fix missing tpm_buf_destroy() in
 tpm2_read_public()

tpm2_read_public() calls tpm_buf_init() but fails to call
tpm_buf_destroy() on two exit paths, leaking a page allocation:

1. When name_size() returns an error (unrecognized hash algorithm),
   the function returns directly without destroying the buffer.

2. On the success path, the buffer is never destroyed before
   returning.

All other error paths in the function correctly call
tpm_buf_destroy() before returning.

Fix both by adding the missing tpm_buf_destroy() calls.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v6.19+
Fixes: bda1cbf73c6e ("tpm2-sessions: Fix tpm2_read_public range checks")
Signed-off-by: Gunnar Kudrjavets <gunnarku@amazon.com>
Reviewed-by: Justinien Bouron <jbouron@amazon.com>
Reviewed-by: Paul Menzel <pmenzel@molgen.mpg.de>
Reviewed-by: Jarkko Sakkinen <jarkko@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jarkko Sakkinen <jarkko@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/char/tpm/tpm2-sessions.c b/drivers/char/tpm/tpm2-sessions.c
index 3b1cf1ca0420..c4da6fde748f 100644
--- a/drivers/char/tpm/tpm2-sessions.c
+++ b/drivers/char/tpm/tpm2-sessions.c
@@ -203,8 +203,10 @@ static int tpm2_read_public(struct tpm_chip *chip, u32 handle, void *name)
 	rc = tpm_buf_read_u16(&buf, &offset);
 	name_size_alg = name_size(&buf.data[offset]);
 
-	if (name_size_alg < 0)
+	if (name_size_alg < 0) {
+		tpm_buf_destroy(&buf);
 		return name_size_alg;
+	}
 
 	if (rc != name_size_alg) {
 		tpm_buf_destroy(&buf);
@@ -217,6 +219,7 @@ static int tpm2_read_public(struct tpm_chip *chip, u32 handle, void *name)
 	}
 
 	memcpy(name, &buf.data[offset], rc);
+	tpm_buf_destroy(&buf);
 	return name_size_alg;
 }
 #endif /* CONFIG_TCG_TPM2_HMAC */
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `drivers/char/tpm/tpm2-sessions.c`

- **Error path for `name_size()` failure**: Added `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf)` before returning `name_size_alg` when `name_size_alg < 0`. This ensures the buffer is released when an unrecognized hash algorithm is encountered.

- **Success path**: Added `tpm_buf_destroy(&buf)` before `return name_size_alg` at the end of the function. This ensures the buffer is destroyed after successfully reading the public data.

### Relationship Between Modifications

Both changes address the same root cause: the function allocates a TPM command buffer via `tpm_buf_init()` but fails to call `tpm_buf_destroy()` on two exit paths, leading to a memory leak. The error path fix prevents a leak when `name_size()` returns an error, while the success path fix prevents a leak when the function completes normally. Together, they ensure that the buffer is always destroyed before returning, regardless of the exit path taken.
